messages:
maya: quick follow-up from the per-layer precision RFC — ran a prototype on the 7B stack with dynamic per-layer profiles. results: aggressive 4-bit on MLPs + fp8 for attention q/k gives ~1.6x throughput, but perplexity increased ~0.6% and a few odd token substitutions in low-prob tails. not catastrophic but non-trivial. thoughts on rollout guardrails?

sam: thanks for the run, maya. can you paste the exact profile you used? curious about q/k quantization and kv cache interactions.

maya: pasted the profile below (prototype config):
```yaml
precision_profile:
  default: int8
  overrides:
    MLP: 4bit
    attn_qk: fp8
    attn_v: int8
  quality_guard: "perplexity_ratio<1.01 && embedding_cosine>0.985"
```

liam: couple quick concerns: 1) fp8 for q/k changes dot-product scaling — we saw small bias shifts that amplify over long contexts. 2) KV cache reuse across requests with different precision settings is dangerous (bit-compat mismatch).

eva: +1 to liam. We should define measurable guardrails, not heuristics. propose these minimal metrics for rollout: token-level KL to baseline, top-3 token overlap, embedding cosine on validation prompts, and a small hallucination-sensitive eval subset.

research-bot: automated evals ran on rfc-eval-1 set: KL=0.013 (baseline 0.01), top3_overlap=0.92, embedding_cosine=0.987, perplexity_ratio=1.006. Hallucination subset error rate increased from 0.8% -> 1.4%.

sam: numbers look borderline but not disastrous. question: runtime complexity for switching precision per-layer at inference? will we need multiple kernels and schedule changes at each layer boundary?

maya: yes, runtime needs per-layer kernel selection. prototype swaps kernels between MLP and attention blocks; cost is small (~2-3ms per sequence on 7B) but increases variance. we can mitigate with grouped layers (apply same precision to a block of N layers) to amortize kernel switch.

liam: we should also think about interface surface: keep model-serving API simple. propose a single optional field on model config: precision_profiles (named list), and allow rollout policies that map traffic buckets -> profile. e.g. stable (int8 default), perf (4bit-MLP), canary (small % with perf profile).

maya: agree. example rollout API (sketch):
```json
{
  "model": "rw-7b-v1",
  "precision_profiles": [
    {"name":"stable","profile":"default:int8"},
    {"name":"perf","profile":"mlp:4bit,attn_qk:fp8"}
  ],
  "rollout": {"policy":"canary","percent":5}
}
```

eva: operational guardrails: require eval pass before enabling >10% traffic, auto-rollback if token-level KL>0.02 or hallucination delta >0.5% over baseline in last 1k requests. also emit per-request quality score so ops can monitor drift.

research-bot: note: quantization calibration matters. static min/max clipping from layer calibration helped int4 reduce outliers but fp8 needs exponent range handling per-channel for q/k. recommend adding per-layer calibration artifacts to model bundle.

sam: good point. where do we store those artifacts? in model registry as separate files versioned with the model?

maya: yes, attach calibration.json to model manifest. manifest example: "calibration: s3://models/rw-7b-v1/calib/v2.json". runtime will fetch at load time. fallback: if artifact missing, use conservative int8 fallback.

liam: one more: caching semantics. we must forbid reusing KV cache generated under different profile unless quantization is lossless/guided. simplest rule: KV cache tagged by profile-id, cache hit only if profiles match. costlier but safe.

maya: agreed. implementation note: tag cache entries with profile hash and model version. infra-bot: queued patch #4821 to add profile-hash to cache key, ETA staging deploy end of week.

infra-bot: patch #4821 deployed to staging at 1782349300, smoke tests passing.

eva: action items: 1) maya -> run wider eval on 70 prompt suite with hallucination-sensitive tests (owner: maya) 2) sam -> design registry schema for calibration artifacts (owner: sam) 3) liam -> add cache-tagging enforcement to runtime (owner: liam) 4) research -> run per-channel range calibration experiments and report delta (owner: research-bot). target: gate for canary in 10 days.

maya: will run evals and post results here. initial impression: perf profile looks promising if we tighten calibration and limit canary to short-context queries initially. :+1:

sam: thanks all. if we keep the rollout conservative and automate rollback, this could be big win on cost.

research-bot: scheduled experiments: per-channel fp8 calibrations across 3 seeds, will post numbers when done.
